deals.headline: Blue Jays unveil $300 million privately funded Rogers Centre renovation
deals.summary: Multi-year, privately funded renovation to turn Rogers Centre from a multipurpose stadium into a ballpark. The release does not state the currency.

deals.date_text: Announced 2026; targeted by first half of 2027
deals.evidence: saying it will sell minority stakes in the portfolio to other investors by the first half of 2027
deals.headline: Rogers plans minority stake sales in Rogers Sports (Blue Jays, MLSE, media)
deals.summary: After completing its purchase of the remaining 25% of MLSE from Kilmer Sports for $4.35 billion, Rogers said it will create Rogers Sports (MLSE properties plus the Blue Jays and other assets) and sell minority stakes in the portfolio, which it values at more than $25 billion, by the first half of 2027. Planned, not completed.

name: Toronto Blue Jays
notes: US/Canadian teams publish no accounts: revenue, player expenses and operating income (EBITDA, net of revenue sharing and stadium debt service) are Forbes estimates for the 2025 season. Forbes states Rogers paid $137M in 2000; no page read states Rogers' percentage (taken to be whole ownership but stake_pct left null). Rogers Centre purchase (2004, $25 million) predates the 2015 deal window. Legal entity, attendance, kit/sponsor and social counts not found on a citable page. The $300M renovation release gives no currency.
ownership_summary: Owned by Rogers Communications, which bought the club in 2000 (Forbes: price paid $137M). In October 2026 Rogers completed its buyout of MLSE and said it will fold the Blue Jays, MLSE and its media assets into a new Rogers Sports unit, planning to sell minority stakes in that portfolio to outside investors by the first half of 2027.
